Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Alsergrund's district crime statistics, reported by meinbezirk.at in May 2025, show car break-ins nearly doubling from 38 to 69 cases between 2023 and 2024, while apartment burglaries stayed roughly stable around 105 cases and bicycle theft fell slightly. In August 2026 a Freedom Party (FPÖ) press statement circulated via the OTS wire cited police figures for around 20 business break-ins across Alsergrund and neighbouring Währing within a few weeks, attributing most to juvenile offenders — a party statement rather than neutral reporting, though based on cited police data. These are overwhelmingly property-crime trends (parked cars, businesses, apartments) rather than street-level offenses against pedestrians, and no documented incidents of violent or street crime affecting visitors turned up for Alsergrund. Daytime is unremarkable in press coverage; the documented rise in break-in activity is mainly relevant after dark and mostly to residents/car owners rather than a pedestrian-safety issue. Sources checked: meinbezirk.at, 13 May 2025 – "Kriminalstatistik: Deutlich mehr Einbrüche am Alsergrund verzeichnet"; OTS (ots.at), 18 Aug 2026 – FPÖ press release: "20 Geschäftseinbrüche in Währing und Alsergrund – ehemals sichere Bezirke werden zum Kriminalitäts-Hotspot".
